description: Critical thermal stress. Immediate physiological risk of severe heatstroke, circulatory collapse, and organ failure with even moderate physical activity.
Dangerous heat load. Core body temperature elevates rapidly during outdoor activity. High risk of heat exhaustion, severe cramps, and heat hyperpyrexia.
Substantial thermal strain. Sweating rate increases significantly; fatigue, dehydration, and reduced physical and cognitive performance occur.
Noticeable heat burden for unacclimatized individuals and those engaging in strenuous physical exertion. Increased fluid requirements.
Thermal comfort / neutral zone. Optimal conditions for normal physiological thermoregulation and regular outdoor or indoor activities.
Mild cold sensation; minimal thermal strain. Light protective clothing recommended during early mornings or elevated terrain.
